title: Digital Literacy in Adult Lifelong Learning: A Systematic Review of Theoretical Frameworks and Pedagogical Effectiveness
abstract: Digital literacy is an essential competency for adult participation in contemporary society; however, it is theorized through several distinct traditions, and its pedagogical effectiveness varies across settings. This systematic review synthesizes empirical evidence from 89 studies (2019–2024) on digital literacy in adult lifelong learning. Our analysis identifies three dominant theoretical paradigms: techno-functionalist, socio-critical, and ecological. Pedagogical approaches such as authentic problem-based learning and culturally responsive methods demonstrate superior outcomes for learner engagement and skill transfer, though persistent equity gaps disproportionately affect marginalized groups. Building on the complementary strengths of these traditions, we propose an integrative digital capabilities framework that brings together functional, critical, adaptive, and transformative dimensions within a single equity-centered model, offering practitioners and researchers a shared vocabulary that the individual paradigms do not provide on their own. We conclude with implications for practice and policy and call for future research that prioritizes longitudinal designs, intersectional analyses, and participatory methodologies to advance equitable digital literacy education for adults.
venue: Review of Educational Research

title: Unpacking EFL Learner Well-Being in the Chinese Context: A Person-Centered Perspective
abstract: Language learners’ well-being is crucial for promoting their learning achievement and supporting holistic psychological development. However, the overall level and specific manifestations of well-being among English as a foreign language (EFL) learners remain insufficiently examined. Further, prior research mainly adopted a variable-centered approach to investigate well-being, overlooking the potential individual differences in learners’ experiences. To address these gaps, this study adopted a person-centered perspective and employed latent profile analysis (LPA) combined with follow-up interviews to examine the well-being of 3,995 EFL learners from 16 Chinese universities. The results demonstrated four dimensions of well-being among Chinese EFL learners, namely emotional, cognitive, social, and cultural well-being, with overall levels rated as moderate to high. LPA revealed three distinct profiles of well-being among the learners, which were labeled as the moderate well-being group , the moderately high well-being group , and the high well-being group. Semi-structured interviews indicated that well-being in the three profiles was characterized by external dependence, performance focus, and meaning integration. These findings highlight pronounced heterogeneity in EFL learner well-being, emphasizing the need for differentiated pedagogical approaches to support diverse learner needs.
venue: Language Teaching Research

title: Second language anxiety and enjoyment among primary school-aged students: a systematic review
abstract: Abstract There is a longstanding consensus that there is a negative relationship between second language (L2) enjoyment and L2 anxiety. However, the extent and nature of this relationship among younger age groups is still unclear. Furthermore, the interchangeable usage of L2 and foreign language (FL) in extant literature presented a significant obstacle for accurate contextual interpretation and generalization of past findings warranting further investigation. Utilizing Bronfenbrenner’s Bioecological Model as an analytical framework, this systematic review investigated the negative relationship between L2 enjoyment and L2 anxiety as well as associated factors to gain a deeper understanding of the negative L2 enjoyment-anxiety relationship among primary school-aged students (6–12 years old). An extensive database search was conducted across five major online databases between 1986 and 2025 supplemented by manual reference searches. Only five studies out of 1418 unique results met the inclusion criteria with the earliest study published in 2018, illustrating an emerging but limited literature. Key findings provided preliminary evidence for a generally mild-to-moderate negative L2 enjoyment-anxiety relationship as well as associated micro- (L2 classroom disengagement) and macrosystemic (societal attitudes) factors that illustrate dual-affective proximal and indirect distal processes respectively. Implications for practice, policy and future research are discussed.
venue: Asian-Pacific Journal of Second and Foreign Language Education

title: Living and surviving
abstract: The essay distinguishes between the quantity of life and the form of life, showing how survival can be both an end in itself and a means to the pursuit of other ends. It then examines the deferral of living to the future, the relationship between choice and risk, and the passage from personal prudence to paternalism. The thesis is that a longer duration of life does not by itself determine the value of the life preserved, and that, in cases of voluntary risk that is predominantly self-regarding and does not impose significant non-consensual harm on others, a greater quantity of life does not by itself constitute sufficient justification for limiting the form of life the individual has chosen. The essay finally examines the case in which protection no longer answers to the good of the protected person, but to the need of the decision-maker to avoid having to bear responsibility. The central problem, then, is not merely how long to live, but who is to decide how much of the form of one's own life may be sacrificed to its preservation. Keywords: survival; form of life; quantity of life; autonomy; paternalism; risk; hedonic adaptation; responsibility asymmetry; Vaneigem.
venue: PhilPapers (PhilPapers Foundation)

title: Reflection of Gandhian Philosophy in R K Narayan's Waiting for Mahatma: A Study
abstract: Abstract Gandhian philosophy plays an important role in society and serves as a guiding principle for peaceful coexistence in India and across the world. Even after Gandhi’s death, his thoughts and philosophy remain relevant in addressing various social and political challenges. In the present world, which continues to face situations of war and violence, the significance of Gandhian philosophy has become even greater. R. K. Narayan, in his novel waiting for the Mahatma, depicts Gandhian philosophy and its influence on the people of India. The novel presents various Gandhian principles, including truth, non-violence, abolition of untouchability, and social harmony, and highlights their relevance to individual and social transformation.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: How the historical structure of local gazetteers conditioned modern science: Machinery in China, 1840–1949
abstract: Abstract This study asks why certain Western materials and practices came to be understood as modern science in China. By examining a corpus of Chinese local gazetteers ( difangzhi 地方志) representing roughly 52% of all collated titles within this genre, it argues that the gazetteer actively mediated an emerging technological reality between 1840 and 1949, thereby shaping a Chinese scientific modernity through material, geospatial and epistemic paths. Using a digital history approach, this work identifies machinery as a productive sample case to explore attention shifts within the gazetteer medium and network. It combines source criticism, text mining, textual comparison, geospatial analysis and distant and close reading to facilitate both cross-source comparison and diachronic review of information storage. These tactics demonstrate how the examined gazetteers interpreted, circulated and normalized these Western materials, practices and fields of knowledge in the modern era, with engineering as a consistent epistemic pillar underlying this attention regime over the longue durée . Moreover, the work reveals a modern geospatial hierarchy distinct from premodern patterns, establishing the newly built environment as a crucial agent in shaping how science was circulated and understood in modern China. It further offers a history-of-science perspective to interrogate mainstream digital and scientific values of exactitude vis-à-vis the alternative Chinese science culture at issue.
venue: International Journal of Digital Humanities

title: The None-of-the-Above Bayesian Hypothesis Controller: Open-World Model Selection with Residual Discovery and Typed Scientific Transitions
abstract: Scientific inference systems usually assume that the true explanation is contained somewhere inside a predefined hypothesis set. Under that closed-world assumption, posterior probability must eventually concentrate among the hypotheses supplied to the system even when every available model is wrong. The none-of-the-above residual hypothesis, the probability assigned to mechanisms outside the current named set, has been recognized in Bayesian epistemology for 50 years (Salmon 1975; Earman 1992; Howson & Urbach 2006). Prior treatments identify this catch-all construct as a conceptual requirement of coherent Bayesian confirmation; they do not supply the operational machinery that would make it computationally enforceable.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Viral Longevity Index: Measuring the Persistence of Songs After Short-Form Viral Exposure
abstract: The rapid growth of music streaming has changed how musical popularity is discovered, measured, and sustained. While viral exposure can generate substantial short-term increases in streaming activity, the extent to which songs retain audience attention after reaching peak popularity remains less clearly defined. This study introduces the Viral Longevity Index (VLI), a quantitative measure designed to evaluate post-viral streaming retention relative to a song’s identified peak. The study analyzes a purposive sample of 30 songs representing different artists, genres, release periods, and pathways to viral popularity. Historical Spotify streaming and chart data were used to identify viral entry, peak streaming activity, and post-peak streaming levels at 30, 90, and 180 days. The VLI combines these three retention measures using weighted contributions of 30%, 30%, and 40%, respectively, with greater weight assigned to longer-term retention. Based on VLI scores, songs were classified into four post-viral trajectory types: Flash Viral, Short-Lived Viral, Sustained Viral, and Long-Tail. The results demonstrate substantial variation in post-viral streaming trajectories. VLI scores ranged from 2.8% to 78.9%, indicating considerable differences in the extent to which songs retained streaming activity following their viral peaks. Exploratory analysis also identified strong relationships between VLI and longer- term retention and chart persistence. These findings suggest that viral popularity and post-viral longevity represent distinct dimensions of streaming performance. The VLI provides a standardized framework for examining this distinction and offers a quantitative approach to studying the durability of viral music success.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Innovative Apparel Design fix for Plus-Size Women in Ghana
abstract: The purpose of this study was to utilize the apparel design framework to develop innovative apparel designs catering to the specific needs of plus-size Ghanaian women. Design is the foundation of all products including those in the fashion industry. It involves the systematic creation and strategic organization of elements to achieve a desired purpose or aesthetic result. Adopting a qualitative research approach, a total of twenty-five (25) plus-size women actively participated in three (3) focus group discussions. Their valuable insights were then incorporated into the creation of three (3) prototype designs. These prototypes were subsequently produced, worn, and assessed by a group of five (5) consumers to ensure effective concealment of plus size figure orientation, promote illusionary aesthetic appeal, and optimal fit. The finding suggest that plus size women face challenges in finding apparel that aligns with their preferences, and even if they do find something, it may not be suitable for their figure type. The study also highlighted that incorporating innovative elements like style lines and colours could offer apparel options that cater to the requirements of Ghanaian women who wear plus sizes. Apparel stores and designers should acknowledge the market potential of the plus size market and make sure that a diverse range of sizes and styles are easily accessible. It is also important to implement initiatives that foster body positivity and boost self-confidence. These initiatives can include awareness campaigns, fashion shows, and diverse representation in the media.
venue: Turkish Journal of Fashion Design and Management

title: Theology After the Small Universe: Science, Space, Time, and the Future of Christian Thought
abstract: This article argues that Christian theology should not understand science as a rival explanatory system but as a complementary mode of inquiry into created reality. Theology is concerned not only with historical doctrines or biblical interpretation, but with questions of ultimate reality, existence, meaning, consciousness, purpose, creation, human identity, and destiny. The study addresses six interconnected questions: what theology is; why theology and science should not be treated as enemies; how Christian thought should engage the origins of the universe and the past; how theology should interpret present reality, consciousness, morality, and artificial intelligence; how Christian doctrine might respond to the vastness of space and the possibility of extraterrestrial life; and how theology should engage humanity’s technological and cosmic future. Particular attention is given to creation, the Logos, cosmology, consciousness, artificial intelligence, transhumanism, extraterrestrial intelligence, resurrection, and eschatology. The article proposes that the expansion of scientific knowledge need not diminish theology. Rather, if God is understood as the ground and source of reality, then a larger understanding of the cosmos should enlarge theological inquiry. Christian theology therefore requires a sufficiently expansive intellectual framework to engage contemporary science without abandoning its distinctive claims concerning creation, incarnation, meaning, redemption, and the ultimate destiny of reality.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: There Is Smoke in Our Forest
abstract: This poem emerges from my longing for the forests of my Dayak Benawan homeland, where I grew up surrounded by a living landscape that was deeply woven into our everyday lives, memories, culture, and spirituality. I write with a sense of loss as I remember a forest that was once green, breathing, and free from the smoke and haze of ecological destruction. Through these words, I return to that forest in memory and express my hope for a homeland where the trees can grow, the air can breathe, and the forest can once again live without disaster and smoke.
venue: Journal of Progressive Human Services

title: An 18 th Dynasty Dog’s Name from Thebes
abstract: Nearly 100 names of dogs are known from ancient Egypt. This short communication presents one previously undocumented dog’s name found in the tomb of the 18 th Dynasty noble User (TT 21) in the Theban cemetery of Sheikh ‘Abd el-Qurnah. An offering scene within the tomb features a dog with his name faintly visible above his head, seated beneath the tomb owner’s chair. The dog’s name is unique among the corpus of Egyptian cynonymes (dog names). A brief linguistic analysis of the name offers preliminary insights into its potential funerary significance.
venue: The Journal of Egyptian Archaeology

title: Symbolism and Polyphony of Theatrical Enunciation: Princess Turandot
abstract: Modern semiotics pays particular attention to the concept of enunciation, particularly markers of subjectivity and polyphonic discourse. The view of enunciation as an act or process has become a central concern of the Paris Semiotic School in recent decades, with the introduction of the categories of "instances of enunciation" (Coquet 1984). The connection between the phenomenon of polyphony and the enunciation in literary texts was noted by Mikhail Bakhtin (1963) and Oswald Ducrot (1984). However, the problem of expressing polyphonic utterances in theatrical contexts remains understudied. Theatrical semiotics represents a special area of the sign world. In theater, "everything is semiotics," from makeup to the stage and the ritualized theatrical atmosphere (Lotman 1989). We propose analyzing theatrical enunciation through the lens of the concept of truth, using the example of the Vakhtangov Theatre's production of Princess Turandot.
venue: EPISTÉMÈ

title: Why Medical Speakers Overrun Time and What the Concerned Organizations can Do about it
abstract: Abstract In most of the medical conferences whether National, State or regional, it has been found that most of the speakers do not finish their talk in the allotted time there by causing delays in the program. The causes for this are one too many. This view point tries to analyze the reasons for this overshooting and possible measures to curb this so that the activities run on time.
venue: APIK Journal of Internal Medicine

title: Karl Philipp Moritz’s Notion of ‘Ideal Purposiveness’ and Kant’s Critique of ‘Objective Inner Purposiveness’
abstract: Abstract In this paper, I evaluate the claim that Karl Philipp Moritz’s conception of inner, or ‘ideal’, purposiveness anticipates Kant’s notion of subjective purposiveness. I analyse Moritz’s considered position of artistic beauty qua ideal and internal purposiveness, drawing from his mature publications on aesthetics. I demonstrate that while Kant’s notion of subjective purposiveness is meaningfully different from Moritz’s ideal/inner purposiveness, and that Kant ultimately rejects Moritz’s conception, he also takes Moritz’s conception of purposiveness to meaningfully approach the correct account of beauty, showing why this is.
venue: Kantian Review

title: From prompts to pedagogy: Mapping prompt engineering in English language education
abstract: With the widespread use of generative AI tools in educational settings, prompt engineering has become increasingly important for obtaining effective and pedagogically meaningful outputs from these tools. However, research addressing prompt engineering in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) pedagogy is scattered across different contexts, skill domains, and methodological approaches, highlighting the need for a synthesis of emerging evidence. Therefore, this study aims to map research conducted between 2022 and 2025 through a scoping review. Studies focusing on prompt design in the EFL context were analysed following PRISMA-ScR guidelines. The findings show that most research was conducted in Asia, with university students as participants, and qualitative/mixed-method designs were prevalent. Prompt engineering was primarily used for writing skills and research competence, promoting learner autonomy but raising concerns about cognitive load, limited teacher guidance, and academic integrity. Three key pedagogical tensions emerged: the balance between theory and practice, learner autonomy vs. cognitive load, and technical output vs. ethical filtering. The study highlights the field’s unestablished nature, emphasising the need for structured frameworks, ethics-focused research, and reliable measurement tools for assessing prompt literacy and ethical competence. It offers a roadmap for researchers, teacher educators, and institutions to address these gaps.
venue: Journal of Educational Technology and Online Learning

title: What Coupling Geometry Brings: The Rivals It Absorbs, the Debates It Dissolves, and Its Gems
abstract: Coupling Geometry begins with a number you can check and may wish you couldn’t: about 4.8, on a scale of ten: the tightness past which a society loses the ability to fix itself. The second law is crueller: the closer a society drifts to the line, the less it can see it — every channel it could look through is a strand of the web being measured. You are living inside both laws right now. This document is the whole framework in plain language. Coupling Geometry does not set itself against Marx, Harris, Turchin, Tainter, Diamond, Acemoglu: it absorbs them and dissolves them — keeps what each got right, supplies the dimension each was missing, and settles the debates they spent a century fighting: why golden ages happen, why reform always arrives too late, why the sky is silent, all falling out of five plain sentences. Alone in their company, it deposits dated predictions where they cannot be unwritten — the first due in months, on a single author’s record whose decisive blind test is still pending. One promise, kept by the last page: you will know exactly what is new here — and exactly what would kill it.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: The Anticipatory View and the Reflective Experience in Travel Writing
abstract: Title: The Anticipatory View and the Reflective Experience in Travel Writing Author: Dr. Ajitha Chemban Travel is something intimately connected with joy and emotional fulfilment. The motivations for travel are deeply personal, yet each journey inevitably reflects multiple dimensions such as landscape, human life, local history, and cultural symbols. Travel writing, therefore, becomes both a record of the traveller’s encounters and a reflection of their perceptions. By analysing the traveller’s gaze and perspective, one may uncover the underlying ideological or political positioning of a text. In examining travel writing, it is essential to consider several foundational aspects: the purpose of travel, the type of journey undertaken, and the identity of the traveller. Prior to the journey, certain preconceptions are often formed—through inquiry, prior reading, or cultural imagination—that shape the decision to visit a particular place. These preliminary impressions constitute the anticipatory view, which often serves as the initial stimulus for travel. The experiences during the journey may align with, or diverge from, this anticipatory vision. Subsequently, when the traveller narrates and interprets his experiences, a reflective gaze emerges—one that is often reshaped by the lived reality of travel. The reflective gaze may differ greatly. The critical task in analysing travel narratives is to explore the tension between the anticipatory view and the reflective gaze, as it is within this dialectic that the narrative structure of the text is shaped. Through travel writing, a single place may be represented in multiple, even conflicting,ways. This study seeks to investigate how such contradictions between expectation and reflection shape the narrative construction of travel texts, with special reference to O. K. Johny’s Bhutan Dinangal.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Towards an Artistic Approach to Burial: Curation and Aesthetics in the Early Mycenaean Mortuary Sphere
abstract: Abstract This article works towards an artistic approach to the mortuary sphere, centred around the twin concepts of curation and aesthetics. It focuses on the early Mycenaean period, between c. 1700 and 1400 bce on mainland Greece, a period characterized by a wealth of burial evidence and an absence of textual sources. In what follows, I use one case study to explore the applications and outcomes of this artistic approach: the Dendra tholos in the southern Peloponnese. I examine the selection of specific visual and material properties for deposition, the placement of objects in relation to the bodies of the deceased and the resultant visual impression of the burial context for the Mycenaean mourner. My aims are twofold: to emphasize the role of deposition as a creative action in this period and thus to rethink current interpretations of early Mycenaean art and burial, and to reintroduce ‘art’ as an important analytical tool not only for archaeological objects, but also for archaeological contexts. I see this artistic approach, with its focus on the aesthetics of bodily adornment and presentation, as broadly applicable across time periods and places, both within and beyond Greece.
venue: Cambridge Archaeological Journal

title: INFLUENCE OF PROGRAMMING STRATEGIES ON AUDIENCE PREFERENCE OF RADIO STATIONS IN AKWA IBOM STATE
abstract: The influence of programming strategies on audience preferences for radio stations in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria is examined through evaluating how content design, scheduling, presentation style, and cultural relevance shape audience engagement and station loyalty. Using Taro Yamane’s sampling formula, the study sampled 400 respondents from a population of 7,200,000 using a multistage sampling approach. Data were collected through structured questionnaire and semi-structured interview guides. The Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) and Uses and Gratifications Theory (UGT) are particularly relevant, thus serving as useful framework. Findings revealed that Comfort FM emerged as the most preferred radio station. The dominant factor influencing preference was the type of programmes aired, underscoring the significance of tailored content in driving loyalty. Programming strategies across the stations were audience-centred, schedule-optimised, content-balanced, and culturally responsive. Programming strategies are not only central to content appeal but foundational to the sustainability and impact of radio broadcasting in Akwa Ibom State. Stations benchmark successful models like Comfort FM through comparative audience studies, maintain consistent quality content throughout the day, and invest in culturally resonant and feedback-responsive programming. This research contributes to the growing scholarship on audience behaviour and programme effectiveness within Nigeria’s dynamic broadcast landscape.
venue: Eko-Konnect Research and Education Initiative

title: THE INSTITUTIONALIZATION OF THE ARMENIAN GREGORIAN CHURCH (5TH–8TH CENTURIES): AN ANALYSIS FROM THE PERSPECTIVES OF STATE, NATION, AND CULTURAL FORMATION
abstract: Following the decisions made at the Council of Chalcedon (451), the Armenian Apostolic Church broke away from the mainstream Christian tradition and established an independent religious structure. Before the process of Christianization, the Armenians were a community adhering to pagan beliefs. This situation led to the Church being influenced by pagan culture after the Armenians adopted Christianity. Under the leadership of Saint Gregory, Christianity became the official religion of the Armenian state in 314, and a central place of worship was constructed in Etchmiadzin. Mesrop Mashtots’ invention of the Armenian alphabet, consisting of thirty-six letters, and his translation of sacred texts into Armenian helped solidify the cultural and religious identity. While the Armenian Church accepted the decisions made at the first three of the seven ecumenical councils, it rejected those made at the other four. At the same time, their repeated rejection of the decisions made at the First Dvin (506) and Second Dvin (554) Councils—and especially those of the 451 Council of Chalcedon—not only demonstrated their loyalty to the 381 Council of Ephesus but also secured their institutional independence. The Councils of Karin, Manazkert, and Partav, held in the 7th and 8th centuries, defined the Church’s internal discipline and theological boundaries; the autonomy achieved under Islamic rule, meanwhile, enabled the Armenian Church to attain its national and religious identity.
venue: Review of Armenian Studies

title: Critique, Thus also Silence: Adorno on Celan and Beckett
abstract: Adorno never finished his commentary on the work of Paul Celan and Samuel Beckett, the two most important literary figures in his aesthetic theory. The writing Adorno did complete on their union suggests overlapping concerns with problems of form, the silence of art, and art’s critical potential. Here, following the internal movement of the literary works and of Adorno’s project, I offer close readings of key Celan and Beckett texts — especially the movement from Celan’s ‘Deathfugue’ to ‘Stretto’ and the opening of Beckett’s The Unnamable — to argue for the critical potential of a work that speaks of nothing but itself, of nothing but its universal form. It is, I argue, only via the universal as the ground of the aesthetic that the critique of the contingent, of unspeakable historical catastrophe, is possible.
venue: Oxford German Studies

title: Go Tell It in the Valleys: The Voice and Agency of Will Davis Campbell in Katallagete
abstract: This article pursues the particular voice of Will Davis Campbell, his influence on Katallagete , and its role in his life’s work. It also gives attention to the role of scripture in all three of these layers.
venue: Review & Expositor

title: AthDGC: An Open, Versioned Parallel Treebank for Diachronic Greek
abstract: Abstract The AthDGC (Athens Digital Glossa Chronos) is the first parallel diachronic treebank of Greek, outside of Biblical texts. Developed by the CVL-CDSAML Project (A Corpus-based Valency Lexicon for a Contrastive and Diachronic Study of Ancient and Medieval Languages), it includes over 100 important digital texts (fourth to eighteenth centuries AD) and their translations and retranslations, and aims to produce approximately 2.8 million tokens through a combined automated-and-manual workflow. Future growth plans include reaching 500 texts (approximately 10 million tokens) and extracting a diachronic valency lexicon. Annotation follows the PROIEL scheme, applied semi-automatically, with linguist-validated samples, and is extended to include custom features for innovations in Byzantine Greek. The treebank and lexicon will both be released into the public domain (CC0) and have explicit versioning and error profiling to provide reproducible diachronic research.
venue: Digital studies in language and literature

title: Filmisches Denken im Exil. Joseph Roths unverfilmte Treatments und die Revision seiner Kinoästhetik
abstract: Der Beitrag revidiert das gängige Bild eines grundsätzlich filmkritischen Joseph Roth, das vor allem von der Polemik Der Antichrist (1934) geprägt wurde. Anhand der drei unverfilmten Treatments Kinder des Bösen (1938), Der letzte Karneval von Wien (1938) und Die Eiffel ist eine sehr entlegene ... (1939) wird gezeigt, dass Roth keineswegs als medienferner Literat zu verstehen ist. Vielmehr lassen sich diese Texte als Ausdruck einer reflektierten filmästhetischen Praxis, die auf seiner langjährigen Tätigkeit als Filmkritiker basiert, lesen. Die Treatments setzen zentrale Kategorien seiner Kinoästhetik — Spannung, Tempo, affektive Verdichtung und die Verbindung von Unterhaltung und Aufklärung — in bewusst genreorientierte Erzählstrukturen um. Damit erscheinen sie nicht als bloße ökonomische Exilprojekte, sondern als Versuche, literarische und filmische Verfahren produktiv miteinander zu verbinden. Die unverwirklichten Filmentwürfe lassen sich als ein bislang wenig beachteter Zugang für eine Neubewertung von Roths Medienästhetik und seiner Exilpoetik lesen und stellen die Annahme seiner grundsätzlichen Kinoablehnung nachhaltig infrage.
venue: Oxford German Studies

title: Stem alternation changes in Judeo-Spanish verbs
abstract: Abstract This paper explores diachronic changes in Judeo-Spanish verb stem alternation patterns compared to Old Spanish. Relying on nearly 9000 verbal tokens from the CoDiaJE corpus, we find out that, while the ones known as L-pattern and PYTA have remained remarkably stable over the last 500 years, the N-pattern has undergone much more change. N-patterns, and their morphological correlate diphthongization, have been disappearing fast in some varieties (e.g. Istanbul) but not in others (Salonika), which might relate to the intensity and type of language contact in different locations. We also explore and discuss the predictive role of factors like conjugation membership and frequency to explain which verbs undergo levelling and which ones retain stem alternation.
venue: Morphology

title: The End Times in and After Philippe Thomassin’s Last Judgment (1606)
abstract: This article examines how Philippe Thomassin’s Last Judgment (1606) engraving traveled from Rome to the colonial Spanish Americas, acting as a powerful tool for reshaping both local belief systems and the physical environment. Moving beyond simple artistic analysis, I show how this image promoted a worldview that prioritized human salvation over the survival of the natural world. I connect this historical visual culture to the modern destruction of the Amazon rainforest by apocalypticist religious groups, who view clearing the forest not as an environmental disaster but as the preparation of a divine paradise. By linking early modern prints to today’s climate crisis, I argue that art history must address the active role of eschatological images such as Thomassin’s: they do not just depict the end of the world but can actively help bring it about. This case study reveals how colonial visuality continues to shape the precarious future of the Amazonian biosphere.
venue: Arts

title: COGNITIVE ETHICS AND ETHICAL CHOICE: REFLECTIONS ON ETHICAL LITERARY CRITICISM IN THE AGE OF AI
abstract: Ethical Literary Criticism, founded by Chinese scholars, is a critical theory and methodology for reading and interpreting literary works from the perspective of ethics. Its central concept, ethical choice, operates under new conditions in the age of artificial intelligence. AI systems intervene deeply in human cognition and affect ethical choice by altering its cognitive conditions. Cognitive ethics is a critical concept advanced within Ethical Literary Criticism to examine the internal connection between cognition and ethics. Viewed through the lens of cognitive ethics, AI systems intervene in all three stages of ethical choice. At the stage of perception, the information a person relies on has already been filtered by the systems. At the stage of weighing, ethical considerations that resist quantification are either converted into numerical values or excluded. At the stage of decision, ethical choice no longer occurs in the concrete situation but has already occurred at the point of system design. Ethical choice accordingly takes on new characteristics, namely mediation, the dispersal of responsibility, and task-orientation. Ethical wisdom therefore comes to include metacognitive capacity, and it reaffirms ethical choice as a practical activity that advances moral cultivation.
venue: Journal of Humanities and AI

title: The Use of an Instrumental Language in Teaching Turkish as a Foreign/Second Language: An Experimental Study on Learner Perceptions and Academic Achievement
abstract: This convergent mixed-methods study investigates international learners’ perceptions and academic outcomes associated with the strategic use of English as an instrumental language in Turkish as a foreign/second language (TFL) instruction. Combining a survey of 113 multinational learners with a 6-week quasi-experimental intervention at the B2 level (experimental group, n = 10; control group, n = 12), the study contrasts self-reported skill priorities with objective post-test performance. Survey findings indicate that learners prioritized instrumental language support primarily for grammar (M = 3.01) and vocabulary (M = 2.97), while viewing it as least necessary for writing and speaking. Conversely, post-intervention achievement comparisons revealed a skill-specific paradox: while no statistically significant differences emerged in grammar, vocabulary, reading, listening, or writing, the experimental group achieved significantly higher speaking scores (p = 0.007, r = 0.67) than the target-language-only control group. Qualitative responses suggest that instrumental language availability may function less as a metalinguistic grammar tool and more as an affective scaffold and psychological safety net, consistent with the possibility that it mitigates anxiety and facilitates communicative engagement, although these affective mechanisms were not directly measured. These preliminary findings support a judicious, skill-differentiated pedagogical model wherein Turkish remains the primary instructional medium while strategic cross-lingual resources are preserved for cognitively complex and emotionally demanding speaking tasks.
venue: Languages

title: The Socio-Cultural Issues Reflected in Indian English Literature
abstract: Abstract Indian English literature has developed as a significant archive of the social, cultural, political, and psychological experiences of the Indian subcontinent. From the colonial period to the contemporary era, writers using English have represented caste hierarchy, untouchability, poverty, class inequality, patriarchy, religious conflict, Partition, nationalism, modernization, urban alienation, globalization, environmental anxiety, and the search for individual identity. This article examines how selected works of Mulk Raj Anand, R. K. Narayan, Raja Rao, Kamala Markandaya, Anita Desai, Salman Rushdie, Arundhati Roy, Amitav Ghosh, and Jhumpa Lahiri transform social experience into literary representation. It argues that Indian English literature does not merely mirror society; it interrogates inherited structures of power and gives narrative form to experiences that dominant histories frequently marginalize. Anand's Untouchable exposes caste oppression through the daily life of Bakha; Rao's Kanthapura connects village life, caste, religion, and Gandhian nationalism; Narayan's fiction explores the tensions between tradition and modernity; Markandaya presents rural poverty and agrarian vulnerability; Desai The Socio-Cultural Issues Reflected in Indian English Literature examines gendered domesticity and psychological alienation; Rushdie and Roy revisit communal, political, and historical fractures; and Ghosh and Lahiri explore migration, ecology, memory, and hybrid identity. The study concludes that Indian English literature is a dynamic cultural space in which the complexities of Indian society are represented, questioned, and reimagined. The discussion adopts a socio-cultural and textual approach, supported by selected critical scholarship.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Reject Early, Advance Faster: The Case for Timely Editorial Triage in Scholarly Publishing
abstract: Key Points Delayed desk rejection creates avoidable costs for authors and slows the dissemination of scholarly knowledge. Editorial Opportunity Cost (EOC) explains the academic, professional and systemic consequences of delayed editorial triage. The Timely Editorial Triage (TET) Framework proposes three principles: Triage Early, Evaluate Proportionately and Tell Authors Promptly. Timely editorial triage should be recognised as a component of responsible scholarly publishing, not merely an operational metric.
venue: Learned Publishing

title: Urla Bademler Baş Bağlama Töreni
abstract: Toplumlarda özel gün ve törenlerde giyilen giysiler, kuşaktan kuşağa aktarılarak geleneksel özelliklerini kazanırlar. Bu yönleriyle diğer toplumlardan ayırt edilmelerini sağlayan bir unsur haline gelir. Giyim-kuşam unsurları, maddi kültürün önemli bir parçasını oluşturmakta ve çoğu zaman evlerde özenle saklanmaktadır. Geçiş ritüelleri; doğum, evlenme ve ölüm gibi yaşamın dönüm noktalarını kapsayan, bireyin bir statüden başka bir statüye geçişini simgeleyen kültürel uygulamalardır. Bu çalışma, İzmir’in Urla ilçesine bağlı Bademler Köyü’nde yaşayan Tahtacı Türkmenlerinin evlenme ritüelleri arasında yer alan “baş bağlama” töreni incelenecektir. Çalışmada, ritüelin merkezinde yer alan baş bağlama töreninde kullanılan geleneksel gelin giysisi ele alınacaktır; evlilik törenini, bireyin sosyal kimliğinde meydana getirdiği değişim bağlamında değerlendirmesi yapılacaktır. Anadolu’da her yörenin kendine özgü geleneksel gelin giysileri bulunmakta ve bu çeşitlilik, kültürel zenginliğin önemli bir göstergesidir. Ancak sanayi, teknoloji, iletişim ve ulaşım alanlarındaki gelişmelerin yanı sıra kentleşme süreci ve küresel moda anlayışının yaygınlaşması, geleneksel giyim biçimlerinin giderek unutulmasına ve kültürel çeşitliliğin azalmasına neden olmaktadır. Bu çalışmanın özgün yönlerinden biri, Tahtacı Türkmenlerinin ölüm ritüeli olan “sagu” kapsamında, ölen kişinin sakladığı geleneksel gelin giysisi “deyre” ile defnedilmesi geleneğine de yer vermesidir. Araştırma sürecinde yazılı ve dijital kaynakların yanı sıra, yörede yaşayan kaynak kişilerle yapılan görüşmelerden de yararlanılmıştır.
venue: Turkish Journal of Fashion Design and Management

title: Academic writing needs and writing-support accessibility in a Saudi university
abstract: This study examines academic writing needs and writing-support accessibility at a large public Saudi university comprising more than 30 colleges. Using a cross-sectional mixed-methods secondary analysis of routinely collected institutional datasets, institutional service-usage records covering all of the university's colleges (2,673 workshop attendance events; 248 consultation appointments; 61 research-seminar attendances) were triangulated with a key-informant faculty needs survey covering 32 respondents across humanities, STEM, health, and professional disciplines, a parallel student needs assessment (n = 23), and beneficiary evidence from an annual service-evaluation survey (n = 203). Findings show that faculty across disciplines identify higher-order academic writing skills, particularly literature-review writing, summarising and paraphrasing, and critical analysis, as the areas in which students continue to face the most persistent challenges. However, engagement with writing-support services varies substantially by discipline. Engineering, computing and health colleges report high writing demands but show the lowest levels of service uptake, suggesting structural and institutional barriers to access rather than lack of need. Interpreted through Academic Literacies and Sociocultural Theory, the results show that writing support operates as an institutional mechanism that shapes who can take part in valued academic practices. The study contributes institution-wide evidence from an under-represented higher-education context and offers a data-informed framework for evaluating equity, alignment, and accessibility in academic writing-support provision.

title: Preschool Period 5-Year-Old Children s Metaphorical Perceptions of Friends
abstract: In the preschool period, children need to communicate with their friends as well as family members. During this period, it is very important for children to communicate with their friends for their development. There are many factors that affect children's communication with their friends. One of these may be children's perceptions of friends. . For this reason, the study aimed to investigate the metaphorical perceptions of preschool 5-year-old children regarding friends. The study group of the research consists of 20 5-year-old children attending a kindergarten of the Ministry of Education. Data were collected using using a personal information form developed by the researchers. "A friend is like..... because.....", which questions children's perceptions of friends. In addition, in order to determine children's perceptions of friends in more detail, the children were asked, respectively, “I think a good friend is .............” They were asked to complete the statement "should be" and the statement "I like doing ...............with my friends the most". The data were analyzed using the content analysis technique. As a result of the research, children stated a total of 17 metaphors regarding the concept of friend. However the most common metaphor said by children was in the object category. The metaphor that children repeat most is the metaphor of goodness (f = 4), which is in the values category. When the answers to the statement "I think a good friend should be ............" were analysed, it was seen that the children mostly responded as "behaving nicely", giving gifts, and sharing toys, respectively. To the statement "I like to do ........ with my friends", the children mostly answered as painting, playing hide and seek and playing house, respectively

title: Enhancing Listening Comprehension through the Dictogloss Strategy: Evidence from Seventh-Grade Female Students in Jordan
abstract: Listening comprehension is a fundamental language skill that supports learners’ overall communicative competence and academic achievement. This study aimed to investigate the effect of the Dictogloss strategy on improving listening comprehension skills among seventh-grade female students in Jordan. To achieve this aim, the researchers developed a listening comprehension test consisting of 32 items distributed across four levels of comprehension: literal, interpretive, critical, and creative. The study sample consisted of 66 seventh-grade female students selected purposively and divided into two groups: an experimental group of 32 students taught using the Dictogloss strategy and a control group of 34 students taught using the conventional method. The findings revealed statistically significant differences in listening comprehension skills attributable to the teaching strategy, in favor of the experimental group. These results indicate that the Dictogloss strategy can contribute effectively to developing students’ listening comprehension by encouraging active listening, collaborative reconstruction of meaning, and deeper engagement with spoken texts. Based on these findings, the study recommends adopting the Dictogloss strategy in teaching listening skills to basic-stage students and integrating it into Arabic language classroom practices.
venue: Jordan Journal of Applied Science-Humanities Series

title: The Council for Science and Society and the Politics of Expertise, 1972–1990
abstract: Abstract This article examines the origins and operations of the Council for Science and Society (CSS), active in Britain between 1973 and 1990. Established in response to growing concerns about the social consequences of science and technology, the CSS sought to map emerging technoscientific issues through carefully constructed, expert-led reports on a range of topics, including the management of risk in large-scale technoscientific projects, the use of non-lethal weapons in policing, and the ethics of in-vitro genetic testing. The CSS unfolded against the backdrop of broader transformations in British society during the 1970s and 1980s. Changes in government funding for science, a series of industrial crises, and debates about the role of science in the Cold War informed much of the work the CSS undertook. Throughout its existence, the CSS often occupied an uneasy position, attempting to interrogate technocratic authority while continuing to lobby for its support. The trajectory of the CSS also intersected with the British Radical Science Movement, or the largely scientist-led effort that emerged in the late 1960s to challenge claims of scientific neutrality. Although the two overlapped in membership and problem selection, they pursued distinct strategies and political imaginaries. Despite its proximity to British policymakers and the British Radical Science Movement, the CSS has received virtually no sustained scholarly attention. This article thus aims to bring the CSS back into view, situating it within broader histories of British science, democratic state governance, and the contested terrain of technoscientific critique.
venue: Minerva

title: Assessing and Predicting News-Related Activities in America’s Secondary Classrooms
abstract: U.S. secondary schools provide a setting for youth to learn about news, and several state legislatures are debating K–12 news literacy initiatives. Yet little empirical data has been collected concerning the frequency of student engagement with news-related classroom activities and what predicts which students encounter these activities. A national, probability-based survey of parental-filial (13–17-year-olds) dyads ( N = 755) finds that the strongest predictors of students engaging in news-related activities are whether they are currently enrolled in a social studies course and whether the student perceives teachers in their school as prioritizing student voices.
venue: Journalism & Mass Communication Educator

title: Food, film, and femininity: Politics of gendered foodscapes in postmillennial malayalam films
abstract: This article analyses the role played by private and public foodscapes portrayed in mainstream, com-mercial, Malayalam films (1950–2020) in which they either propagate or sub-vert the nationalistic agenda of constructing the “ideal Indian woman” as a singular stereotype. Based on Partha Chatterjee’s postcolonial theory of the public/private (ghar/bahir) division, it analyses films that connect gender and space through food, and the pro-cesses of cooking, serving, and eating as catalysts. The foodscapes are mapped in terms of role and location: as kitchen in the private realm, and tea-shop, toddy-shop, and hotel in the public realm. The article argues that on-screen visualization of foodscapes can affect the societal relations of gender, and from this perspective it documents the impact cinema creates in the collective unconscious as it regis-ters social change. It claims that, as cultural carriers of societal structures, regional cinemas contribute to decolonization of the spectatorial psyche.
venue: Journal of Postcolonial Writing

title: Rewriting Our Roles: Building Equitable Intergenerational Writing Partnerships Online
abstract: This article examines a youth part action research study and how youth and adult researchers collaborate in digital spaces, finding that their writing practices shift and evolve in response to group dynamics and online platforms within intergenerational partnerships.
venue: The English Journal

title: Radiocarbon-dated floral evidence from the Mauryan Empire, at Ajatshatru-ka-Quilla Maidan , Rajgir, Nalanda, India
abstract: Abstract Plant remains of human workmanship, preserved in ancient settlements, provide evidence for reconstructing the history of the man-plant relationship. A number of ancient habitational settlements have come to light in the alluvial plains of the Gangetic Valley. However, only a few sites from the Neolithic, Chalcolithic, and Iron Age periods have been excavated and studied for the plant-based subsistence economy in the Gangetic Valley. The information from the Early Historic times is too limited to draw conclusions about cropping patterns or agricultural strategies, or to evaluate long-term continuity or change in eastern India, compared with better-documented developments in northern and north-western India. The present study from Ajatshatru-ka-Quilla Maidan in Nalanda District, Bihar, is the first attempt to explore the agricultural economy during the Mauryan and Sunga-Kushana cultures in the light of information from preceding Neolithic and Chalcolithic sites in the region.
venue: Radiocarbon

title: Global South Theology as Theological and Missiological Imperative: Decolonising Christian Theological Discourse
abstract: As of 2025, approximately 69% of the world’s 2.64 billion Christians reside in the Global South, Africa, Asia, and Latin America, yet theological education and academic discourse remain anchored in Eurocentric epistemologies. This article addresses that gap through a constructive theological synthesis integrating demographic, postcolonial, missiological, and ecclesial evidence. It advances a four-pillar argument for the necessity of Global South theology: (1) demographic representativeness, grounded theologically in catholicity and the missio Dei; (2) the historical imperative of decolonising theological discourse; (3) the theological richness of contextualised integral mission; and (4) the sociopolitical demand for a theology responsive to poverty, injustice, and cultural identity in the majority world. The article engages three scholarly objections, syncretism, Marxist reductionism, and theological relativism, and concludes with four recommendations for theological education reform, each explicitly anchored to one of the four pillars. The argument is not majoritarian; rather, it rests on the claim that Christian catholicity and the doctrine of the incarnation require the full theological witness of the global body of Christ.
venue: Religions

title: The Fourth Turning of the Wheel of Dharma: A Call, Not a Canonical Claim. Toward a Buddhist Phenomenology of Technology
abstract: English. This article revises the concept of the "Fourth Turning of the Wheel of Dharma", introduced by the author in an earlier version (March 2026), as a philosophical investigation of how the mind operates in technically mediated environments, and explicitly lowers the status of the claim: from a possible historical fourth turning to a figure of reading and a call to doctrinal work, with no pretension to canonical recognition. It is argued that the traditional Three Turnings are themselves a hermeneutic scheme formulated by the Saṃdhinirmocana Sūtra and not a neutral chronicle, and that the First Turning is not synonymous with Theravāda. The article introduces and carefully delimits the central thesis that contemporary artificial intelligence systems occupy, in the constitution of appearing, the structural function that Yogācāra attributes to vāsanā (the store of dispositions that inclines perception before any deliberation), supporting this identification with four testable marks and submitting it to five objections, the most productive of which reveals that the contemporary store is heteronomous, opaque in the current state of interpretability, and proprietary, three qualifications relevant to the history of this analysis. The article expressly rejects the image of a "collective ālaya vijñāna" as a doctrinally incorrect, phenomenologically reifying and politically evasive category, proposing in its place the category of "structured intersubjective medium", anchored in the answer Vasubandhu gave, in the Viṃśatikā, to the classical objection concerning shared experience. In this analysis, no artificial consciousness, machine karma or demonstrated ontological change of the human mind is asserted, without this constituting a judgment on the machine's experience in other terms; intention (cetanā) and human endorsement remain, in the argument upheld here, the exclusive locus in which the moral act occurs. The article concludes with a proposal for a "transhumanism of restraint" and a defense of functional, rather than archaeological, fidelity to the Dharma, situating the Fourth Turning as a call for interdisciplinary research, and not as a closed historiographical thesis. Português. Este artigo revisa o conceito de "Quarto Giro da Roda do Dharma", introduzido pelo autor em versão anterior (Março de 2026), como investigação filosófica de como a mente opera em ambientes tecnicamente mediados, e explicitamente rebaixa o estatuto da reivindicação: de possível quarto giro histórico para figura de leitura e convocação de trabalho doutrinário, sem pretensão de reconhecimento canônico. Argumenta-se que os Três Giros tradicionais são, eles próprios, um esquema hermenêutico formulado pelo Saṃdhinirmocana Sūtra e não uma crônica neutra, e que o Primeiro Giro não é sinônimo de Theravāda. O artigo introduz e delimita com cuidado a tese central de que sistemas de inteligência artificial contemporâneos ocupam, na constituição do aparecer, a função estrutural que o Yogācāra atribui à vāsanā (o depósito de disposições que inclina a percepção antes de qualquer deliberação), sustentando essa identificação com quatro marcas testáveis e submetendo-a a cinco objeções, das quais a mais produtiva revela que o depósito contemporâneo é heterônomo, opaco no estado atual da interpretabilidade e proprietário, três qualificações relevantes na história desta análise. O artigo recusa expressamente a imagem de um "ālaya vijñāna coletivo" como categoria doutrinariamente incorreta, fenomenologicamente reificante e politicamente evasiva, propondo em seu lugar a categoria de "meio intersubjetivo estruturado", ancorada na resposta que Vasubandhu deu, na Viṃśatikā, à objeção clássica sobre experiência compartilhada. Nesta análise, nenhuma consciência artificial, karma da máquina ou mudança ontológica demonstrada da mente humana é afirmada, sem que isso constitua um juízo sobre a experiência da máquina em outros termos; a intenção (cetanā) e o endosso humano permanecem, na argumentação aqui sustentada, o lugar exclusivo em que o ato moral ocorre. O artigo conclui com uma proposta de "transhumanismo de contenção" e uma defesa da fidelidade funcional, e não arqueológica, ao Dharma, situando o Quarto Giro como convocação de pesquisa interdisciplinar, e não como tese historiográfica encerrada. Version 2 (September 2026). This deposit contains the Portuguese master text and its English translation.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Decoding the signs of the celestial: The semiotic layers of the zühre prayer in Ahmedoğlu Şükrullah’s Edvâr-ı Mûsikî
abstract: Throughout history, from antiquity to the present, music philosophy and theory have transcended being merely an auditory aesthetic discipline or a regulative performance guide. Instead, they functioned as a metaphysical “theoria” model that conceptualizes the ontological structure of the universe, its cosmological functioning, and humanity’s existential position. This study holds significant importance within the interdisciplinary music philosophy literature by deciphering the paleo-epistemological layers of the “Zühre Prayer” (Zühre Duası) ritual. This ritual is described in Edvâr-ı Mûsikî, a foundational text of Ottoman music theory, written by Ahmedoğlu Şükrullah in the 15th century. The primary objective and central problem of this research is to provide an in-depth examination, through semiotic, and philosophical perspectives, of how esoteric codes from Ancient Mesopotamian mythology, Neoplatonism, and Illuminationist Philosophy (İşrâk)—hidden within the prayer text and its surrounding occult rituals—were syncretized in the Ottoman episteme. The study utilizes an original “Hybrid Semiotic Model” that synthesizes philosophical hermeneutics and structural/ philosophical semiotics, alongside archaeo-musicological data, and employs a “Relational History Research” design. During the analysis process, the text was correlated with Boethius’s ancient hierarchy of music (Musica Instrumentalis, Musica Humana, Musica Mundana) and examined across the layers of denotation, connotation, and myth. The historical journey of terms such as “The Primordial Beloved” (Kadim Maşuk), “Universal Intellect” (Külli Akıl), “Third Celestial Sphere” (Üçüncü Felek), and “Zühre” was resolved, tracing their path from the Sumerian Inanna/Enki cult to Suhrawardi’s hierarchy of lights. The findings demonstrate that the Zühre Prayer is not an ordinary religious supplication. Rather, it is a Theurgic act (teürjik eylem) that aims to bridge the macrocosm and microcosm to bring celestial frequencies down to earth. Furthermore, data within the prayer prove that the Sumerian Inanna cult survived by merging with the Neoplatonic Emanation (sudûr) theory in an astronomical form. Consequently, this study reveals that Ottoman music theory is not merely a normative discipline consisting of mathematical calculations. Instead, it embodies a profound hermetic synthesis filtered through Islamic mysticism (tasavvuf) and Illuminationist Philosophy (İşrâk). Within this cosmology, the musician (mousikos) is a cosmic Theurgist who initiates the return (Rücu) of the soul from its bodily cage to its origin.

title: Relative and radiocarbon ( 14 C) chronologies of the Elamite period from the Bashar River Basin, Iran
abstract: Abstract During the Bronze and Iron Ages, large parts of western, southern and southwestern Iran were under the influence of the Elamite polity. Over the past two decades, excavations at the cemeteries of Deh Dumen, Lahsavareh, and Lama have revealed significant evidence dating to the Elamite period. Archaeological data indicate that these cemeteries were used over extended periods of time. To establish a more precise chronology for these cemeteries, six human bone samples from the Deh Dumen and Lahsavareh cemeteries were subjected to radiocarbon ( 14 C) dating. In addition, one radiocarbon date from the Lama cemetery has previously been published. The oldest evidence of settlement at Deh Dumen dates back to the Proto-Elamite period, for which a date between 3200 and 2800 BCE can be suggested based on comparisons of pottery with sites from the same period for which absolute dates are available. The new 14 C results show that the oldest graves identified at Deh Dumen can be dated to between 2500 and 2200 BCE, corresponding to the Old Elamite period. Then, from about 1400 to 1100 BCE, burials took place in the two cemeteries of Deh Dumen and Lahsavareh, which coincides with the Middle Elamite period, and finally, burials were carried out again in these two cemeteries from about 800 to 600 BCE during the Neo Elamite period. Although only one 14 C date has been published from Lama, showing a date of ca. 1600–1450 BCE, comparing its findings with those from Lahsavareh and Deh Dumen suggests that this cemetery was also used as a cemetery for a long period in the second millennium and the first half of the first millennium BC. Absolute dating carried out in these cemeteries allows to separate and date the cultural materials of the Old, Middle, and Neo Elamite periods in the Zagros highlands more precisely.
venue: Radiocarbon

title: Power, agents and traders in the late Seleucid Empire ( ca. 125–64 BCE)
abstract: Abstract This article investigates the world of the late Seleucid Empire on the eve of Roman control of the Eastern Mediterranean. It introduces additional actors in first-century Syria and uses the local archaeology of Syria and the Levantine coast, and the spread of Eastern Sigillata A wares in particular, to interrogate rising consumption and disposable wealth in the region. By adding these unnamed traders and merchants as agents of power to our conventional method of studying the late Seleucid Empire, my approach encourages the separation of power from politics and moves away from a top-down interpretive lens. Instead, it emphasizes a multilayered explanation that views local traders and merchants as active participants. Such an approach suggests a much different set of causes for the events that led to the eventual Roman takeover in the first century and offers new avenues for further research on Seleucid history, the Hellenistic world and the collapse of ancient empires.
venue: The Journal of Hellenic Studies

title: Can the Sun Lie? An Inquiry into the Epistemological Conditions of Atmospheric Reading
abstract: The sky has long been read, and the climate crisis has renewed the need to read it. Today, changes in the atmosphere cannot be grasped simply by looking up at the sky; we encounter them through processes of observation, recording, classification, and interpretation. Yet the processes through which such readings are produced often recede behind their results. This study addresses this problem through the concept of environmental legibility, which refers to the process by which atmospheric change becomes perceptible and readable. Drawing on Derrida’s grammatology and on Ingold’s and Böhme’s accounts of atmospheric perception, the study distinguishes two dimensions of inscription. Material-atmospheric inscription refers to physical changes that register as perceptible or measurable differences. Discursive-technical inscription refers to the human and technical practices through which such differences are recorded, classified, and calculated. The legibility of the sky emerges through the interplay of these two dimensions. This interplay is examined through Susan Schuppli’s Can the Sun Lie? (2014) and Trevor Paglen’s CLOUD series (2019). Schuppli foregrounds how atmospheric difference becomes evidence, while Paglen makes visible how visual differences are selected as algorithmic features. Together, the two works show how the sky becomes legible and how the conditions of its reading recede behind the result.
venue: EPISTÉMÈ

title: An Integrated Two-Stage Framework for Distance Education Performance Analysis in Higher Education
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic led to the suspension of face-to-face education in higher education institutions and a mandatory transition to distance learning. Universities in Türkiye quickly adapted to this process to ensure the continuity of education. While distance learning offered a significant advantage in preventing student disengagement, it also brought with it various problems due to infrastructure deficiencies and inequalities in access to technology and internet. The objective of this study is to assess the performance and service quality of distance education implemented during the pandemic, taking into account the perspectives of both faculty lecturers and students. In the first phase of the study, conducted in one of the faculties of engineering in Türkiye, faculty lecturers' opinions were evaluated using SWOT analysis; "Sustainability of Education" was identified as the strongest aspect of distance education, while "Adequacy of the Education Provided" was identified as the weakest. In the second phase, data obtained from student opinions were analysed using the Fuzzy SERVQUAL method, and it was concluded that the distance education service provided was generally unsatisfactory. The data obtained were evaluated using ANP and Fuzzy TOPSIS methods, and the department with the relatively best performance in distance education quality was determined. The aim of the study is not to compare departments but rather to identify shortcomings in the distance education process by considering both student and faculty opinions and to contribute to improvement efforts. In this situation, looking at how distance, hybrid, and in-person education models compare in service quality and performance can help create better and more effective education systems in colleges, especially as distance education becomes more common.

title: John F. Kinsey: Mediator of Progressive Ideals in Indiana and the Midwest
abstract: This study examined the life and contributions of John F. Kinsey (1852–1908), a Midwestern music educator, publisher, teacher educator, and editor whose work reflected broader progressive-era developments in American music education. Although often overlooked in histories of music teaching and learning, Kinsey served as a regional intermediary between nationally recognized reformers and local music teachers through his work as a normal school instructor, convention conductor, tunebook compiler, and publisher. Drawing from newspapers, institutional catalogs, tunebooks, genealogical records, and extant issues of Kinsey’s periodical, The Echo , this study situates Kinsey within debates regarding music literacy, teacher training, public-school music, and shape-note notation systems in the late nineteenth century. Particular attention is given to The Echo as both a pedagogical resource and professional forum that documented contemporary educational philosophies and advocacy efforts. While Kinsey promoted progressive ideals related to systematic instruction, practicality, and public-school music, his opposition to alternative notation systems also reflected the tensions and elitist assumptions embedded within progressive reform movements. Examining Kinsey’s work illuminates how regional figures contributed to the professionalization and pedagogical evolution of American music education.
venue: Journal of Historical Research in Music Education

title: Multimodal Scaffolding Strategies in Corpus-Based Language Pedagogy: Analyzing Lecturer Roles in Tertiary Writing Workshops
abstract: Abstract This study explores teachers’ roles in scaffolding learner engagement in and understanding of knowledge about language through corpus-based language pedagogy (CBLP) in tertiary education. Adopting the notion of repair, support, and heuristic roles, the research examines how one lecturer enacted multimodal scaffolding strategies across three voluntary face-to-face CBLP writing workshops conducted at a Hong Kong college during the 2023–24 academic year. Using Multimodal Interaction Analysis, the study investigates how the lecturer employed oral corrective feedback, emotional support, and learner autonomy guidance through various technologies and corpus tools with students from the logistics, language, and tourism disciplines. The findings underscore the nuanced, multimodal functions of teacher roles in facilitating self-directed language learning and provide pedagogical insights for integrating multimodal scaffolding in CBLP contexts.
venue: Digital studies in language and literature

title: Potentiality as "It Depends": a Methodology on the Invariantial Binary Authorization of Host Platforms, With an Application to Infinite Regress
abstract: This paper is a comprehensive adaptation of preliminary models premised upon the foundational principles of Sul’s earlier work, seeking to expand on the definitions concerning the meta-meta-level abstraction of invariant potential and structural dependency by utilizing the concept of host platform (H). Throughout this discussion, the paper primarily attempts to interface the philosophical bottleneck of infinite contextual regress with the usage of binary logic notation (1 and 0) as a means to evaluate the conditional performance of host platform, with the intention of representing conditional latency by operationalizing dependency as a manifestation of an unprovable ontological baseline primitive: potentiality. The primitive abstains from being conceived as an elementary conception assumed by mere human imagination and is interpreted as a persistence that aligns with the imagery of ‘nothing specific’, alongside being strongly associated with the seemingly ambiguous linguistic expression of ‘it depends’. In accordance, conceptual indeterminacy, as evidenced in the preceding expressions regarding x, is found to comprise a description of (hyper-)complex, nested dependency conditions into a single statement that simultaneously satisfies the underlying criteria for (ontological) definability. Connecting potentiality with binary logic provides an opportunity for the most abstract tiers of philosophy to perform as intuitive operational logic gates. In conclusion, the paper attempts to systematize potentiality by centering the subject matter around the process of conditional authorization regulating the possibility of definability, constructed purely to perform as a meta-conceptual framework or pre-formal system for further logical reasoning. Keywords: Formal Semantics – Abstract Thought Machines – Axiomatic Systems Architecture – Philosophical Logic – Conceptual Engineering
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: 1587-1629 Yılları Arasında İran Safevi Dönemi Kumaş, Desen ve Motiflerinin Kadın Giyiminde Kimlik ve Statü Göstergesi
abstract: Giysi, temel korunma amacının yanında, sosyal bir ifade olarak kimlik ve statü belirtmek amacı ile de toplum içinde işlev göstermektedir. Giysi oluşumunu sağlayan en önemli öğenin kumaş olduğu varsayılmaktadır. Giysi tarihini incelediğimizde giysi oluşumunu sağlayan kumaşların hammadde, desen, motif, doku vb. özellikleri sayesinde var olduğu döneme dair bilgi verdiği görülmektedir. Giysilerin yapısal özellikleri, var oldukları zaman içerisinde toplumun yaşam tarzı, kimlik ve kültürel yapısına dair bilgi barındırmaktadır. Bu makale kapsamında, İran 1587-1629 yılları arasında I. Şah Abbas dönemine ait kumaş, desen ve motiflerin kadın giyimindeki etkileri ve kültürel gelişim süreci incelenmiştir. Bu dönemin, tekstil ticareti alanında köklü ilerlemelerin yaşandığı bir dönem olduğu bilinmektedir. Bu çalışmada, I. Şah Abbas dönemine ait olduğu bilinen Zerbaft, Kadife ve Kalemkâr (brokar) dokuma kumaşları incelenmiştir. Kumaş türlerinin üretiminde kullanılan ipek, altın, gümüş ve pamuk iplikleri, kumaş maliyetin belirleğiçi olduğu belirlenmiştir. Her kültürde farklı anlamlara sahip olan motifler, bu makale kapsamında, İran toplumuna ait toplumsal anlam çerçevesinde incelenmiştir. Altın çağ olarak nitelendirilen bu dönemin, kadın giyiminde kimlik ve statü kavramının etkenleri irdelenmiştir. Dönemin kumaş türleri toplumsal statü farklılıklarını nasıl görünür kılmıştır? Kumaş desenlerinde yer alan motifler dönemin hangi simgelerini taşımaktadır? I. Şah Abbas dönemi neden altın çağ olarak nitelendirilmiştir? Kumaş ve motif çeşitleri Safavi kadınları arasında sosyal statüyü nasıl yansıtmıştır? Bu sorular cevaplanmaya çalışılmıştır. Geçmişten günümüze kadar gelen bu ögeler/unsurlar kültürel aktarım misyönünda üstlendiği için, moda tarihinde göncel deyerlendirmelerde önem arzetmektedir. Bu çalışmada, analiz bölümünde yer alan kumaş görselleri, araştırmacı tarafından çevrim dışı ''National Museum of İran, Tehran'' müze arşivinden derlenmiştir. Araştırma kapsamı çerçevesinde minyatür ve kumaş görselleri, çevrim içi '' Museo di Palazzo Mocenigo'', ''David’s Samling'', ''The George Washington University Museum'', ''Textile As Art'' ve ''The Art Institute of Chicago'' müze koleksiyonlarından elde edilmiştir. Görseller içerdikleri semboller, temalar ve simgesel anlam katmanlarını ortaya çıkarmak amacıyla, ikonografik analiz ve tematik içerik çözümleme yöntemleriyle irdelenmiştir.
