title: Fractured allegiances: teacher identity, curriculum policy, and ideological negotiation in Iranian English language education
abstract: Curriculum policies are enacted not only through official texts but also through teachers’ interpretation of competing ideological, pedagogical, and professional expectations. This qualitative study examines how Iranian English language teachers experience and negotiate these tensions within an ideologically contested curriculum context. Using narrative inquiry and visual identity mapping, data were collected from 18 EFL teachers in public and private educational settings through semi-structured interviews, critical incident reflections, and identity mapping activities. Thematic narrative analysis identified four interconnected dimensions of teachers’ experiences: fragmented professional identity, strategic policy enactment through adaptation, emotional labour and moral tension, and reflective reconstruction of professional purpose. Integrating policy enactment theory, teacher identity scholarship, discourse-oriented perspectives on ideological dimensions of language education, and emotional labor research, the study distinguishes between fracturing as the curriculum-mediated process through which competing ideological, pedagogical, ethical, and professional commitments are brought into tension and fractured allegiances as the condition that may result when teachers’ attempts to reconcile these commitments remain incomplete. The findings demonstrate that curriculum is actively constituted through teachers’ identity work and professional judgement rather than policy compliance alone. Although situated in Iran, the study offers a conceptual framework with implications for curriculum policy, teacher education, and professional support in ideologically complex educational settings.
venue: Journal of Curriculum Studies

title: THE FUNCTION OF LANGUAGE AND LITERARY DEVICES IN PLOT CONSTRUCTION IN AGATHA CHRISTIE'S WORKS
abstract: This article examines the role of language and literary devices in constructing plots in Agatha Christie’s detective fiction. Particular attention is paid to dialogue, repetition, irony, ambiguity, contrast, ellipsis, and narrative perspective. Through examples from The Murder of Roger Ackroyd, Murder on the Orient Express. The study demonstrates how linguistic choices function not merely as stylistic decoration but as mechanisms for concealing clues, directing suspicion, creating suspense, and preparing the final revelation
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Visualising Language: Isibheqe Sohlamvu and the Decolonisation of Design Education
abstract: This article examines the practical outcomes of integrating the Isibheqe Sohlamvu writing system into jewellery design education, focusing on a second- year class project at the University of Johannesburg in 2022 that encouraged students to incorporate Indigenous knowledge into their design processes. Through a focused artefact-based analysis of one student’s jewellery studio design journey, the study explored how Isibheqe Sohlamvu, a contemporary visual writing system developed in the 2010s for Southern Bantu languages, can support culturally situated conceptual development within studio practice. The visual logic of Isibheqe offers a relational and symbolic approach to form- making that contrasts with alphabet-based conventions, positioning Indigenous epistemic frameworks as generative resources for design education. The article argues that within the limits of a single case and artefact-based analysis, integrating Isibheqe Sohlamvu could contribute to more inclusive and context- responsive pedagogies in higher education.
venue: de arte

title: Reflections and remembrances at the end of a very long chapter
abstract: As the end of decades of directing the CIIS Drama Therapy Program approaches, program founder and director Renée Emunah reflects on the program’s inception and evolution, why teaching and academia held her interest, and how running a graduate program was interwoven with other contributions to the young drama therapy field.
venue: Drama Therapy Review

title: Where the Pressure Falls: Ten Conceptions of the Ultimate Ground, Compared
abstract: Conceptions of what is explanatorily last are defended and attacked in conventional pairs — theism against naturalism, panpsychism against physicalism — and are rarely compared as a field. This paper compares ten, each read from a single text in which a competent contemporary defender states it at its strongest, against seven questions argued to be those any such conception is obliged to answer: the existence of a concrete domain, its order, subjects, modality, value and norm, the distribution of suffering, and the distribution of epistemic access to the ultimate. Conceptions are ranked only by dominance — better on at least one question and no worse on any — so that every verdict survives any admissible weighting of the seven and every incomparability records that the difference turns on weights rather than on evidence. Of the ten, two are undominated: Tegmark's mathematical universe and Della Rocca's Spinozism, which share no subject matter but share a structure, each deriving its assessed coverage from a single principle. Undominated is a weaker standing than it sounds, and is not a claim that either is true or best: it means only that nothing in the field matches them everywhere and exceeds them somewhere, and the word covers two different cases — one of the two outranks eight of the nine others, while the other outranks two and is incomparable with seven. None of the four theistic conceptions in the field survives undominated. Being outranked here is a relation between what two conceptions reach, and three things follow from that and are meant strictly: this is not a finding that theism is false, since a conception may reach less than a rival and be true while the rival is false; it is not a finding that theism is improbable, since no probability is assigned to anything; and it is not a finding that holding a theistic conception is unreasonable, since what a person is entitled to believe turns on grounds the study does not weigh. Nor is theism displaced where a reader of the literature would expect. On a statement of the data that does not presuppose the point at issue, neither the distribution of suffering nor the distribution of belief generates a debit against any conception in the field, and every theistic conception is already outranked on the earlier questions alone. They are displaced earlier, over what the world is and how it hangs together. The paper reports what the result rests on, what would overturn it, and where the instrument used was never exercised.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: CODA: The Calculus of Obstruction, Descent, and Authority
abstract: CODA: The Calculus of Obstruction, Descent, and Authority A measurement can erase a distinction that matters to the question being asked. A repair can make a local calculation look better while leaving a different obstruction untouched. CODA asks what can actually be concluded once the states, observation, query, repair family, and decision rule are named. It begins with a witnessed difference between two states. Algebra, distance, and permission enter only when additional structure is supplied. The paper gives a precise criterion for when a query descends through an observation: it must give the same answer on every observation fibre. A collision supplies a concrete obstruction. Finite repair menus expose the limits of claims based on exhausted searches, while a finite-dimensional quotient measures what admitted linear repairs cannot remove. Primal repairs and dual bounds provide checkable certificates in stated cases. Exact examples distinguish an exact repair, a coherent residual, and a nonclosed defect. Other examples show locally solvable constraints with no global solution and finite samples that agree while their continuous integrals differ. CODA also maps eight companion research components into one carefully scoped account. FOC studies repair quotients; MUR and OR study re-presentation; CS, CS_Q, and Q separate finite observations from continuum claims; A records typed leftovers; FDA studies evidence-derived standing conditions. GTLA organizes how evidence and separately supplied grants are kept apart. These are roles and declared interfaces, not a proof that every component has one universal implementation. The release includes a claim ledger, exact finite code, a walkthrough notebook, figures, and a local Lean development. The ledger separates mechanized statements, prose proofs, calculations, policies, historical reports, and open problems. A preserved historical point-span construction is explicitly refuted as a faithful groupoid embedding. The proposed faithful replacement, broader continuum programme, and any grant of external authority remain open. The result is a usable map of what the current evidence supports and where a new argument is still needed.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Şair ve Patron Arasında Şahane Bir Kelime: Teşrîfin Türk-Fars Edebî Literatürlerindeki Karşılıkları Üzerine
abstract: Bu makale, klasik Türk ve Fars edebiyatlarında şair-patron ilişkisini yeniden düşünmeyi amaçlayan kavramsal bir anahtar olarak “teşrîf” terimini merkezine almaktadır. Osmanlı saray protokolünde; hilat ve ihsân bağlamlarında kullanılan teşrîf, edebî himaye sisteminde şairlere verilen maddi ve sembolik armağanları karşılayan bir üst kavram olarak ele alınmaktadır. Çalışmada önce Osmanlı ve Fars lügatleri taranarak teşrîfin tarihî ve ıstılâhî anlam katmanları ortaya konulmuş; ardından Türk ve Fars klasik şiirinden seçilen örnekler üzerinden kelimenin şiir dilindeki işlevleri karşılaştırmalı biçimde incelenmiştir. Klasik dönemde Osmanlı ve İran sahasında yaşamış pek çok şairin metinlerinden hareketle teşrîfin yalnızca “hilat” ile sınırlı kalmadığı; altın, gümüş, at, kürk, taç, silah, zahîre, makam ve itibar gibi farklı ihsan biçimlerini kapsayan dinamik bir gösteren olduğu anlaşılmaktadır. Makale, teşrîfin padişahın dönüştürücü kudretini görünür kılan sembolik bir araç olarak şairin toplumsal konumunu belirlediğini; methiye üretimiyle ödül ekonomisi arasında süreklilik kurduğunu ileri sürmektedir. Böylece edebî patronaj çalışmalarına yeni bir terminolojik ve yorumsal çerçeve önererek şair-hami ilişkisinin yalnızca biyografik değil, kavramsal bir düzlemde de okunabileceğini savunmaktadır. Bu yönüyle çalışma; disiplinlerarası yaklaşımla tarih, sözlükbilim ve şiir incelemesini buluşturarak literatürde eksik kalan bir kavram alanını görünür kılmayı ve yeni tartışmalara zemin hazırlamayı hedeflemektedir.

title: Scientific Epistemic Metrology (SEM): Discipline Spine v0.5
abstract: Scientific Epistemic Metrology (SEM) is a development-candidate discipline proposal concerned with the traceability, calibration and bounded standing of scientific claims as they move through observation, representation, computation, interpretation, comparison and succession. SEM begins from a jurisdictional premise: science may reason far beyond direct perception, but whatever standing a scientific claim acquires must remain recoverable to the physically instantiated information, operations, exposure conditions and representations through which that standing was earned. SEM therefore does not attempt to measure Reality or truth directly. It proposes instead to measure the integrity of the scientifically recoverable relation between evidence, operation, representation and claim. The paper develops a typed rather than scalar approach to epistemic calibration, including traceability, exposure fidelity, operational adequacy, referential fidelity, scope fidelity, provenance continuity, residual preservation and successor discipline. It introduces the Scientific Epistemic Measurement Event (SEME), the associated Scientific Epistemic Measurement Record (SEMR), and distinguishes these from the earlier Dot Theory Seme: a claim-bearing informational object capable of carrying semantic entitlement between scientific operations. SEM is positioned within the wider Dot Theory research programme at dottheory.co.uk and in developmental relation to the Canonical Constitutional Record (CCR), Constitutional Physics: Scholarly Positioning and Comparative Literature Review (CP-SPLR-001), and F O R M / Constitutional Verification Protocol (CVP). These relationships establish provenance and methodological context; they are not presented as independent validation of SEM. This v0.5 publication is deposited as a Development Candidate. It proposes a domain, vocabulary, candidate measurands, calibration operations, failure conditions and research programme sufficiently explicitly for independent criticism, comparison and testing. If the proposed irreducible function of SEM collapses entirely into existing disciplines, its claim to separate disciplinary standing should be abandoned rather than preserved by terminology alone. title: Husserl on Cartesian Evidence: A Textual and Phenomenological Reappraisal
abstract: Abstract Following Descartes, Husserl assigns a pivotal epistemological, methodological, and ethical role to evidence within the framework of his radical rationalism. At the same time, however, he repeatedly criticizes Descartes’ theory of evidence, on two principal counts. First, he rejects what he takes to be Descartes’ circular attempt to justify the epistemic value of evidence by recourse to metaphysical considerations, namely the existence of a veracious God; second, he maintains that Descartes fails to provide a precise phenomenological characterization of evidence, reducing it to a mysterious feeling. The aim of this paper is to reassess these two criticisms. On the one hand, by returning to Descartes’ texts, I argue that he does not ground the validity of evidence in God’s veracity; on the other hand, I suggest that Husserl’s second objection can be turned back against his own position, insofar as his concept of apodictic evidence remains phenomenologically underdetermined.
venue: Journal of Transcendental Philosophy

title: An erotic embrace: Mina Loy, Marcel Duchamp, and the dynamics of legacy
abstract: Addressing the long obfuscation of Mina Loy’s visual art, even as her poetry has gained traction among scholars, this study explores Mina Loy: Constructions, organized by Marcel Duchamp, Julien Levy, and David Mann at the Bodley Gallery in New York in 1959. The analysis reveals Duchamp’s deep investment in the exhibition and the active role Loy played in its development. Undertaken at a moment when both artists were profoundly concerned with the dynamics of legacy, the show reveals the close parallels in their practices. It lays bare their common interest in the fourth dimension, which framed a collaboration that can be understood in those terms as an “erotic embrace.” Mina Loy: Constructions represented a complex conceptual endeavour that further catalyzed the development of the “new kind of picture” – as Loy put it – that she had conceived in New York and nurtured in Aspen, the implications of which are, in many ways, only now becoming visible.
venue: Feminist Modernist Studies

title: Maharshi Panini and Education: Re-envisioning linguistics within the Indian
abstract: Maharshi Panini, the distinguished grammarian of ancient India, holds a prominent place in the history oflinguistics and the Indian intellectual tradition. His principal work, the Acmādhyayī, presents a highlysystematic, rule-governed account of Sanskrit and has attracted sustained scholarly attention from linguists,philosophers, historians of language, and computational linguists. Beyond its role as a grammatical treatise,the Paninian tradition offers valuable insights into systematic classification, economy of expression, rulebased reasoning, and structured knowledge transmission. This study investigates Panini’s contributions tolinguistic theory and explores selected pedagogical implications of his grammatical framework forcontemporary education. Additionally, it situates Panini within the Indian Knowledge System and considersthe potential relevance of Paninian principles to modern language pedagogy and multidisciplinary learning.Employing a qualitative, review-based methodology, the study analyses books and peer-reviewed scholarlypublications on Paninian grammar, linguistic theory, phonology, computation, and Indian approaches tolanguage and education. The study examines the literature through interpretive and comparative analyses.The scholarly review indicates that the Acmādhyāyī demonstrates a highly formal organisation, sophisticatedrule interaction, economy of expression, and generative characteristics. Research on the Śiva Sūtras andpratyāhāra system further underscores the significance of systematic sound classification and economicalrepresentation within Pāninian grammar. Contemporary scholarship has also explored the relationshipbetween Panini an grammar and formal computation and compared aspects of the Indian grammaticaltradition with modern phonetic and phonological theories.

title: Auditable Admissibility: Ultimate Explanation and the Selection of Candidates
abstract: Recent grounding-theoretic work has produced increasingly rigorous certifications of rival ultimate explainers — necessary beings, autonomous essences, trans-categorial grounds, strongly well-founded structures — while the most developed comparative methodology for global theories, Oppy's virtue-theoretic naturalism, acknowledges the incompleteness of its own metric across multi-dimensional trade-offs. We argue that this acknowledged limit becomes acute precisely where the later grounding-theoretic candidates would have to be compared, and that the two literatures fail to mesh for a structural reason. Distinguishing three tasks — structural admissibility, candidate identification, and cross-framework selection — we show that every account examined here resolves, defers, asserts, or concedes the third task without an articulated account of the transition from intra-framework certification to cross-framework selection under conditions of policy disagreement. Our central claim: if cross-framework selection is to represent rather than merely dissolve disagreement, it requires an explicit admissibility policy whose commitments are publicly auditable and dialectically revisable; the accounts examined here leave that policy implicit, defer it, or defend it only within the framework whose candidates it licenses. The paper introduces the concept of an admissibility policy — the entry conditions, explanandum registry, and translation rules that constitute any comparison's space — and specifies the minimal representational architecture such a policy requires, including a detachable instrument, dual-ledger cost accounting, without prejudging how comparative judgment then falls.

title: Locational analysis of late Holocene archaeological settlements in the lower Paraná fluvial system: The role of geomorphology and resource distribution
abstract: Research in the South American lowlands has grown considerably alongside the incorporation of new technologies and analytical methods. Nevertheless, studies focusing on site location and associated settlement patterns in the region’s extensive wetlands remain limited. This paper presents the results of the first locational analyses, using GIS-based analysis to assess topographic prominence, visibility to and from the sites, and geomorphological classifications, from 86 archaeological sites in the alluvial plain and island sectors of the lower Paraná River. The aim was to evaluate the extent to which these factors have influenced site location and distribution, and by extension, the decision-making underlying subsistence practices and territorial organisation. The results show that sites occupy the highest ground, although their relative altitude does not differ significantly from that of the surrounding terrain. We interpret these locations as choices made for protection against periodic flooding, while remaining close to shallow lakes zones where resources were concentrated. Visibility from sites drops off with distance, reaching no more than 10 km. More than 90 % of the sites are visible from the fluvial network, indicating intervisibility between settlements and the fluvial network within a 5000 m radius. This may suggest a pattern of territorial organisation more closely linked to the riverine transport network. Visibility from each site to the surrounding landscape appears to be closely linked to resource availability, whereas visibility of sites from the fluvial network is more closely tied to control and territorial organisation. By contrast, intervisibility among sites—understood as landmarks—may be connected to memory and ancestral ties, contributing to group identity and belonging.
venue: Journal of Archaeological Science Reports
